answers.question: Who are we allowed to hire under immigration law?
answers.content:
The company hires only United States citizens and aliens who are authorized to work in the United States, and it does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of citizenship or national origin (Immigration Law Compliance, JBA Policy Manual p.9 [p.9]).

The compliance piece that sits with you at the salon:

- Under the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, every newly hired or rehired employee must, as a condition of employment, complete the Employment Eligibility Verification Form I-9 and present documentation establishing identity and employment eligibility (Immigration Law Compliance, JBA Policy Manual p.9 [p.9]).
- New hires must present on their start date a voided check or direct deposit form from their bank, along with the necessary copies of their identification according to the I-9 — if those items aren't presented on the start date, all training stops until the employee can present the proper documentation (Orientation, JBA Policy Manual p.33 [p.33]).
- Employees with questions about immigration law issues are encouraged to contact Human Resources, and may raise questions or complaints about immigration law compliance without fear of reprisal (Immigration Law Compliance, JBA Policy Manual p.9 [p.9]).

The manual doesn't spell out which specific documents satisfy the I-9 list or the federal completion deadlines — if you need that detail for a particular hire, HR is the right call (jbahr@Glowbrands.com).

answers.question: Who is eligible for PTO and when does it start?
answers.content:
**Who's eligible** — All salaried managers, full-time corporate office personnel, and full-time Assistant Salon Directors/Assistant Makery Managers. PTO is not issued to temporary or contract employees.

**When it starts** — Accrual begins after 90 days of employment in that position.

**What they accrue** [S6]:
- 90 days – 4 years full-time: 2 weeks (80 hours), accrual cap 120 hours
- 5–9 years full-time: 3 weeks (120 hours), cap 160 hours
- 10+ years full-time: 4 weeks (160 hours), cap 200 hours

Unused PTO carries over year to year, but once someone hits their tier's cap, accrual stops until they use some and drop below it.

A couple of things worth knowing alongside that: PTO covers vacation, personal time, personal illness, and time off to care for dependents — it replaces separate sick, absence, personal and vacation time. Salaried employees schedule it in half-day (4 hour) or full-day (8 hour) increments, requests go in at least two weeks ahead, and no PTO is permitted during Sun Tan City's peak season of February 1 to June 1. Only one team member per location is approved off at the same time unless the supervisor says otherwise.

Note that this eligibility list doesn't cover hourly Tanning Consultants — myGlow has a separate non-PTO-eligible time off request path for them, which records the time off but isn't paid. If you need the specifics for a particular person's situation, tell me the role and I'll point you to what's there.

answers.question: Are beards allowed?
answers.content:
Yes. Facial hair is acceptable as long as it is clean, well-groomed, and trimmed (Facial Hair, JBA Policy Manual p.16 [p.16]).

That sits inside the broader expectation that employees keep a neat, clean, professional appearance at all times, and anyone violating the dress code may be sent home to change into proper work attire and may be subject to disciplinary action up to and potentially including termination (Dress Code for The Company, JBA Policy Manual p.15 [p.15]).

So the standard is grooming, not length — if a beard is unkempt, that's the coaching conversation, not the beard itself.
sources: Page 15 Dress Code for The Company

answers.question: Where should employees park?
answers.content:
Employees are not allowed to park directly in front of the location — the spaces closest to the front are reserved for customers. Employees should park farther out ("Employee Parking", JBA Policy Manual p.18 [p.18]). Worth noting for the team: the company assumes no risk or liability for theft or damage to employee vehicles or their contents while on company property ("Employee Parking", JBA Policy Manual p.18 [p.18]).

One related point if you're reviewing parking with staff — smoking and vapor products are not permitted anywhere on the premises, including the parking lots ("Smoking/Vaping", JBA Policy Manual p.12 [p.12]).

answers.question: How much PTO does a full-time manager get in their first years?
answers.content:
For a qualifying full-time position, PTO starts accruing after 90 days in that position, and salaried managers are among the eligible groups [p.41]. From 90 days through 4 years of service in a full-time position, the accrual is 2 weeks (80 hours), with a maximum accrual cap of 120 hours [p.41]. That steps up to 3 weeks (120 hours) at 5–9 years, cap 160 hours, and 4 weeks (160 hours) at 10+ years, cap 200 hours [p.42].

Two things worth flagging alongside it:

- Unused PTO carries over year to year, but once someone hits their tier's cap, accrual stops until they use some and drop back below it.
- Salaried employees must schedule PTO in half-day (4 hour) or full-day (8 hour) increments, and no PTO is permitted during the Sun Tan City peak season listed as February 1 and June 1 [p.42]. Requests should go into the Personnel System at least two weeks in advance [p.42].

Cites: "Provisions", JBA Policy Manual p.41 [p.41]; "Eligibility", JBA Policy Manual p.41 [p.41]; "Usage", JBA Policy Manual p.42 [p.42].

answers.question: Do employees get time off for jury duty?
answers.content:
Yes. Employees who need time off for jury duty are granted the accommodations afforded them under the laws for their area ("Jury Duty", JBA Policy Manual p.47 [p.47]). A few specifics:

- The employee must show the jury duty summons to their supervisor as soon as possible so schedules can be adjusted ("Jury Duty", JBA Policy Manual p.47 [p.47]).
- As the supervisor receiving the summons, you must reach out to Human Resources for guidance on handling the request ("Jury Duty", JBA Policy Manual p.47 [p.47]).
- The leave is paid — normal salary or hourly compensation for up to 15 days. After 15 days the employee can use PTO or take unpaid leave ("Jury Duty", JBA Policy Manual p.47 [p.47]).
- The employee is expected to sign over to the Company any paycheck received from the courts for those first 15 days ("Jury Duty", JBA Policy Manual p.47 [p.47]).
- They're expected to report for work whenever the court schedule permits, or if dismissed from jury duty ("Jury Duty", JBA Policy Manual p.47 [p.47]).

If someone brings you a summons, the first move is to get the copy from them and loop in HR before you commit to anything on the schedule.
